focus: Fetch mechanic vs missing child route

route_status.proven_scope: The unchanged probe_fetch run passed on Godot 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf. Its retained log records aim → fly → fetch → pickup → return twice and END game= won=true at frame 312 with zero misses.
route_status.route_gaps: This is a dormant activity, not a demonstrated child route. main.gd builds friends as a data-only roster after retiring the reef friend pillars (1984-1995); the probe itself selects the fetch record and calls _start_game directly (probe_fetch.gd:13-22). The only _start_game call sites reviewed are the Day One dust-boss handoff and the Chapter Two rainbow-slide helper (main.gd:6753, 7080), neither of which launches Fetch. No visible Wacky/Chuck entry, routed touch, natural exit/re-entry, or ordinary save lifecycle was exercised.
route_status.normal_route_status: DORMANT; source mechanics exist behind the internal launcher, but child reachability is not shown by the minigame catalog row or this probe.

code_constants.value: Aim sweep angular rate = 0.9 * pow(0.72, miss_count) radians per game second; safe-side sweep width is 1.25 initially, 0.85 at two misses, and 0.55 at three or more misses.
code_constants.scope: Code values only. The green interval varies with miss count and is not a fixed child wait.

code_constants.value: pickup_t starts at 0.8 seconds; ball attaches at pickup_t <= 0.35 seconds; Chuck movement is capped at 40 world units per game second.
code_constants.scope: Source constants, not observed real-time timing; the probe runs Engine.time_scale = 6.

timing.assumptions: No child-session duration or seconds-per-probe-frame estimate is reported. The helper's 10.469-second wall time is only probe execution time.

tactile.target_size: No routed touch target was measured. The game labels the action THROW in the aim phase (scripts/main.gd:8375-8385); physical hit size and phone projection remain unknown.
tactile.press_response: In code, the action press starts the ball's fly phase and hides the arrow in the same tick (scripts/games/fetch.gd:246-256). The headless run does not establish rendered-frame response or device latency.
tactile.drag_hold_release: No drag or release gesture is authored for aiming; the player waits for the moving safe cue and presses THROW. The handler reads the action as a held level while aim is active (scripts/games/fetch.gd:246-249); probe_fetch forces action_down false outside aim (probe_fetch.gd:32-36), so held-through-flight behavior is untested.
tactile.ownership: No pointer/touch ownership is exercised. Probe input is assignment to touch_ui.action_down, not an InputEventScreenTouch trace (probe_fetch.gd:32-36).
tactile.cancellation: Pause, focus-loss, exit cancellation and stale-action behavior are not asserted by probe_fetch.

play_appeal.agency: Hypothesis: choosing a safe throw moment gives a simple, repeatable choice; the probe's synthetic tap schedule does not establish that a child reads the cue or feels in control.
play_appeal.variety: Two rounds repeat the same throw-and-retrieve loop. A splash widens and slows the safe area, but there is no distinct second verb or authored dog acting visible in the inspected source.
play_appeal.world_response: Hypothesis: the shrinking safe-side challenge and a visible, animated Chuck could make the throw feel connected to a friend. Current source creates an empty Node3D Chuck root with a null AnimationPlayer, so the visible retrieval response is not established.
play_appeal.replay: Not assessed; this probe ends when the second round wins and does not test an ordinary child-facing replay or return route.

play_sequence.scope: The first six beats reconstruct the exact probe stimulus and phase waits, not a child playthrough. The last two state the concrete routed appeal test still needed.

beats.wait: Probe waits two process_frame calls after instantiating main, calls _skip_intro, waits one process_frame, directly selects the fetch friend record, then calls _start_game and waits one process_frame (probe_fetch.gd:4-22).
beats.input: No routed user input; direct internal launch.
beats.expected: Initial aim phase; the retained log records f=1 phase=aim round=0 miss=0.

beats.wait: While phase is aim, sample every frame; use the current aim_dir and frame counter. No fixed human wait is defined by the source.
beats.input: Set touch_ui.action_down true exactly when aim_dir is nonzero, aim_dir.x < 0.1, and fcount % 12 < 6; otherwise false (probe_fetch.gd:32-36). This is synthetic held state, not a tap event.
beats.expected: First throw; log changes to fly at f=65.

beats.wait: Release the synthetic action immediately after aim; wait for the ball landing and fetch/pickup/return phases, with no input during those phases (probe_fetch.gd:35-37).
beats.input: None until phase returns to aim.
beats.expected: Log records fetch at f=102, pickup at f=108, return at f=128, then aim round=1 at f=140.

beats.wait: Again sample aim_dir once per frame; safe cue dwell is continuous and miss-dependent (fetch.gd:219-245).
beats.input: Repeat the same exact action_down condition as beat 2; release outside aim.
beats.expected: Second throw; log changes to fly at f=234.

beats.wait: Wait without action through landing, pickup and return (probe_fetch.gd:35-37).
beats.expected: Log records fetch at f=271, pickup at f=282, return at f=302, then win at f=312.

beats.wait: For a future child test, wait for the visible green/safe arrow and its transition chime; no fixed seconds are promised.
beats.input: One brief finger press on the visible THROW control; lift before the ball lands.
beats.expected: Determine whether the child connects the cue to the throw without reading the caption or adult prompting; not tested here.

beats.wait: If the child throws into the lake, wait through the splash message and for the next aim cue.
beats.input: No corrective input during the splash; then one new press when the safe cue appears.
beats.expected: Determine whether the child stays willing to retry and understands the broadened safe area; no miss path occurred in this probe.

beats.wait: After retrieving the second ball, allow the friend response and return/exit choice to appear.
beats.input: No adult prompt; observe whether the child asks to play again or chooses a clear exit.
beats.expected: Concrete appeal test: with the live route exposed, have a non-reader play the full two-round loop on the target phone, including one natural miss if it occurs; note cue comprehension, voluntary retry/replay, confusion, and any adult help. No such child test was run.

observations.title: The exact probe reaches both fetch returns through its synthetic schedule
evidence: audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L39/attempt_1/receipt.json: status PASS; exact Godot version 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf; isolated profile; headless=true; rendered_mobile_acceptance=false.

audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L39/attempt_1/probe.log: f=1 aim; f=65 fly; f=102 fetch; f=108 pickup; f=128 return; f=140 aim round=1; f=234 fly; f=271 fetch; f=282 pickup; f=302 return; END game= won=true frames=312.
scripts/probe_fetch.gd:23-40 shows the bounded loop, aim-only input schedule, terminal win check and 40-second frame cap.
observations.reproduction: Use the retained attempt_1 receipt command; the single authorized run exited 0 with no failure lines and the log ended won=true. The script sets Engine.time_scale=6 and synthesizes action_down, so this is a mechanic/state-transition pass only.
observations.child_impact: This proves the scripted safe throws can complete two rounds. It does not prove that a child can find the route, make the timed choice, or understand the resulting ball movement.
observations.proposed_repair: Do not change the mechanic based on this pass. First establish a child-visible route and collect routed/device evidence.
observations.acceptance_test: A fresh ordinary profile enters via a visible route; a routed one-finger test observes both intentional safe throws and at least one zero-input leg, then confirms only intentional play completes.

observations.title: The probe bypasses the ordinary route and touch system
evidence: scripts/probe_fetch.gd:13-22 searches main.friends, chooses the fetch record and invokes main._start_game(fr) directly.
scripts/probe_fetch.gd:32-36 assigns touch_ui.action_down from aim_dir and frame count rather than dispatching a touch event.
scripts/main.gd:1984-1995 describes and builds the friend roster as data-only after reef pillars/beacons were retired; main.gd:7870-7887 starts the requested game only after receiving a record.
scripts/main.gd:6753 and :7080 are the reviewed _start_game call sites: Day One's dust-boss handoff and the rainbow-slide helper, not Fetch.
observations.reproduction: Inspect the direct friend-record selection and _start_game call in probe_fetch.gd; trace current _start_game call sites and the data-only friend roster. The master scorecard also marks Fetch dormant and recommends a Canvas timing surface (MASTER_AUDIT_2026-08-09.md:601-605). No exact active finding for a current Fetch child route was found; MA-2D-002 overlaps its spatial implementation, not this reachability assertion.
observations.child_impact: A child cannot benefit from a passing internal mechanic probe if no ordinary play surface exposes Wacky and Chuck or launches their game.
observations.proposed_repair: Keep Fetch explicitly dormant until there is an authorized, child-visible entry and return path; then review the complete interaction in that route before claiming it is playable.
observations.acceptance_test: On a fresh profile with no debug calls, reach Fetch through an ordinary visible route using one finger, hear/see its instruction, complete or kindly retry, leave, and re-enter with progress and other activities preserved.

observations.title: Chuck's runtime root has no visible body or animation player
evidence: scripts/games/fetch.gd:172-180 creates a bare Node3D root, adds it to main, stores it as chuck, and explicitly stores chuck_ap as null; no visual child is constructed in this block.
scripts/games/fetch.gd:195-198 only plays an animation when the stored player is non-null and has that animation.
scripts/games/fetch.gd:289-322 describes and computes pickup, carrying and return around the Chuck root, then advances the round.
observations.reproduction: Source inspection: the only Chuck node in FetchGame.build is Node3D.new() with no mesh/sprite child; chuck_ap is null, making _chuck_play a no-op. This runtime has no captured visual state.
observations.child_impact: The described dog pickup/run/wag cannot currently be verified as visible, so ball motion may look detached or self-propelled and the friend payoff may be missing.
observations.proposed_repair: When Fetch is commissioned for conversion, use an approved suitable Chuck source in the true-2D Canvas implementation and give each pickup/carry/return a readable contact and settle state; preserve protected friend art.
observations.acceptance_test: At runtime, frame-step and play at full speed through throw, pickup, carrying and return; Chuck must visibly contact and carry the ball with stable identity and readable endpoints, then pass actual phone and owner review.

observations.title: Current mechanic remains a spatial 3D arena rather than accepted 2D play
evidence: scripts/games/fetch.gd:11-17 creates MeshInstance3D, BoxMesh and StandardMaterial3D snow/lake surfaces; :182-189 creates a 3D arrow.
scripts/main.gd:8708-8738 builds the shared spatial arena and fetch-specific 3D environment.
audit/MASTER_AUDIT_2026-08-09.md:601-605 labels Fetch dormant and calls for a generous one-finger Canvas timing surface; active parent finding MA-2D-002 remains IN_PROGRESS.
observations.reproduction: Trace FetchGame.build and _enter_arena for game=fetch; both use Node3D/MeshInstance3D and spatial material/environment code. No Canvas implementation was found for this route.
observations.child_impact: The spatial aim and swimming-era setup carries device and tactile/readability risk under the project's true-2D and one-finger requirements; no target-device evidence is available for it.
observations.proposed_repair: Do not revive the legacy spatial implementation. Any future authorized Fetch work should rebuild the bounded timing verb on Canvas using the accepted medium and art rules.
observations.acceptance_test: The converted Canvas activity must pass focused input/progression/passive/teardown/save probes, aspect-ratio runtime captures, actual M11 touch/performance checks, and separate child/owner reviews.

observations.title: Mercy widens the safe throw while preserving the child's next action
evidence: scripts/games/fetch.gd:219-228 reduces sweep rate after each miss and makes the safe sweep width 0.55 after three misses.
scripts/games/fetch.gd:281-286 gives a kind shake-off retry line after three splashes and returns to aim; it does not throw automatically.
scripts/games/fetch.gd:246-252 requires the action press before entering fly.
observations.reproduction: Code path only; the L39 probe had zero misses and did not execute the splash or three-miss assist branches.
observations.child_impact: If the cue is legible, the forgiving widening window can preserve a route after a miss without removing the child's choice to press again. Child comprehension and appeal are untested.
observations.proposed_repair: Retain the no-punishment, non-automatic mercy design during any future authorized conversion; verify the messages and cue in context.
observations.acceptance_test: Through routed touch, intentionally make one and then three safe-side misses; confirm kind feedback, slower/wider cue, continued child-controlled throws, and no loss or automatic win.

observations.title: The cue has visual and audio components in code, but its child meaning is unverified
evidence: scripts/games/fetch.gd:190 presents the text instruction to avoid the lake and press on green; :231-245 colors and swells the arrow and plays a chime on transition to safe snow.
scripts/main.gd:8375-8385 labels the contextual action THROW during aim.
The L39 log contains phase changes only; it has no rendered capture, audio playback assertion or routed touch trace.
observations.reproduction: Inspect the arrow/cue path and the log. The probe's synthetic condition uses aim_dir.x < 0.1 directly, so it does not show that a player can distinguish the green safe window or hear the chime.
observations.child_impact: If green/red or the chime is hard to notice at phone scale, a non-reader may throw randomly or need an adult to interpret the caption.
observations.proposed_repair: No cue redesign is justified by code alone. Validate the current redundant cue on the actual device through the authorized live route before proposing a change.
observations.acceptance_test: With captions ignored, the child independently points to or presses on the safe cue, sees the ball land on snow, and can recover after a miss; separately verify two-frame response and audible cue on the target phone.

strengths.claim: The safe cue combines a changing visual arrow with a transition chime, and the action is explicitly labeled THROW in aim.
strengths.evidence: scripts/games/fetch.gd:231-245; scripts/main.gd:8375-8385. Code evidence only; cue legibility, audio audibility and child comprehension were not measured.

strengths.claim: The mercy branch slows/widens the safe interval after misses but still waits for an intentional action press, preserving a completion choice.
strengths.evidence: scripts/games/fetch.gd:219-252, 281-286. The L39 probe completed with zero misses, so miss recovery is source-only evidence.

strengths.claim: The internal happy path advanced through two complete round states and terminated with a win without changing the probe or production source.
strengths.evidence: audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L39/attempt_1/probe.log: phase trace and END game= won=true frames=312.

acceptance_gaps: Fetch remains dormant: no ordinary child-visible route or routed-input proof was found; the probe launches it by direct internal method call.
The passing probe forces action_down from simulation state and does not test genuine touch targeting, ownership, hold-through-transition, release, pause/focus loss or cancellation.
Chuck has a bare spatial root and null animation player in this source; no rendered capture establishes a visible pickup/carry/return payoff.
Current implementation is spatial 3D legacy debt; strict true-2D, Mobile visual, phone hit geometry, latency, frame pacing and audio audibility remain unproven.
No child observation establishes cue comprehension, discoverability, comfort, session length, voluntary retry/replay or appeal; no owner acceptance is implied.
